scope: contracts/MaonoVault.json - regenerated from the source by scripts/build-maono-artifact.mjs
audit.method: local deterministic Foundry harness; no live deployment, RPC, fork or real funds
audit.question: Can combinations of individually valid operations cause the vault's economic accounting to diverge from actual economic reality?
audit.answer: No. Across 159 tests, no sequence of valid operations made totalAssets() diverge from the vault's ERC-20 balance or left a claim unbacked. The material risks are depositor liveness (owner-controlled indefinite freezes), protocol revenue (the payer of the monthly fee administers its own invoice) and a broken integration layer.

findings.title: emergencyWithdraw sends 100% of depositor assets to the owner EOA while shares remain outstanding
findings.actor: owner (== manager, the key used by server/blockchain.ts)
findings.root_cause: emergencyWithdraw(uint256) is onlyOwner and transfers assets to owner(); no share burn, no treasury destination, no timelock, no cap
findings.mitigation: route emergency funds to daoTreasury, gate behind timelock+multisig, separate the automation key from the owner key, cap per-period withdrawals
findings.phase2_reclassification: emergencyWithdraw does not exist in MaonoVault_Phase1B. Re-verified exhaustively by phase2 test_ScenarioG_NoOwnerPathMovesTheUnderlyingAsset. Remains a live HIGH for any deployment running the archived legacy bytecode.

findings.title: MTAA upkeep discount is an instantaneous balance snapshot and is flash-loanable
findings.violated_invariant: fee charged equals advertised fee; discounts reflect sustained MTAA holding
findings.root_cause: discount = min(50, sqrt(balanceOf(msg.sender)/1e18)*2.5) read inside the fee-charging call; no time-weighting, lock or snapshot; curve saturates at 400 MTAA
findings.related: the nominal price is unreachable even for an honest owner: holding the 15 MTAA needed to pay already grants a 7% discount (13.95 MTAA charged)
findings.mitigation: time-weighted or staked balance with a minimum lock, or snapshot balances at period start; exclude same-block acquisitions
findings.phase2_reclassification: Still valid against the canonical source; quantified in phase 2 (50% of the nominal annual fee, zero capital at risk) by test_ScenarioD_AcquireDiscountRepayLoopOverTwelveMonths.

findings.title: Shares are minted from the requested amount rather than the amount actually received
findings.actor: any depositor, conditional on the listed asset
findings.root_cause: no balanceBefore/balanceAfter measurement; fee-on-transfer and rebasing assets credit more than the vault receives

economics.protocol_user_loss: 1% of every deposit, compounding across depositors

findings.mitigation: mint from the measured balance delta; explicitly reject fee-on-transfer/rebasing assets in the factory allowlist
findings.phase2_reclassification: Only reachable if a fee-on-transfer or rebasing asset is listed; the asset is fixed at initialize() by the factory, so this is an asset-listing constraint.

findings.title: pause() and hibernation freeze depositor exits indefinitely at zero cost to the owner
findings.actor: vault owner (hibernation also reachable through mere delinquency)
findings.violated_invariant: depositors can always exit a solvent vault
findings.root_cause: all four ERC-4626 entry points carry whenNotPaused and onlyActive; no pause time limit, no guardian, and only the owner can leave hibernation
findings.mitigation: keep withdraw/redeem available while paused, bound the pause duration, and let anyone pay the reactivation fee
findings.phase2_reclassification: Still valid; strengthened by P2-2, which measures the cost asymmetry (22.5 MTAA to freeze depositors for a year vs 180 MTAA to stay compliant).

findings.title: Large withdrawals return a non-zero value while transferring nothing; queued requests are unvalidated and can be permanently unfulfillable
findings.root_cause: above largeWithdrawalThreshold, withdraw() records a request without burning shares or validating the amount; fulfilment requires previewWithdraw(amount) shares, which rounds up

economics.impact: stuck requests, false success reported by server/blockchain.ts; funds still redeemable through sub-threshold redeem()

findings.mitigation: revert or emit a distinct pending event instead of returning a non-zero value; escrow shares at request time and settle against the escrow
findings.phase2_reclassification: No withdrawal queue exists in the canonical source.

findings.title: previewNAV() reports an unbacked manager-controlled number
findings.violated_invariant: reported NAV is backed by assets
findings.root_cause: previewNAV() returns lastNAV verbatim; server/vaultAutomation.ts surfaces it to users

economics.off_chain_impact: arbitrary reported performance (10000e18 real vs 1000000e18 reported in the test)

findings.mitigation: report totalAssets() for on-chain value, bound per-update deltas, display real and reported values separately
findings.phase2_reclassification: No NAV accounting exists in the canonical source.

findings.title: server/vaultAutomation.ts calls distributePerformanceFee, which does not exist on the deployed contract
findings.violated_invariant: the backend's contract API matches the deployed ABI

economics.impact: every performance-fee distribution reverts; the configured 15% performance fee is never collected

findings.mitigation: add the function or remove the call path; add an ABI-conformance check in CI
findings.phase2_reclassification: Broadened in phase 2: the deploy scripts are broken too, not just the automation.

findings.title: Donation griefing can round a victim deposit to zero shares
findings.violated_invariant: a non-zero deposit mints non-zero shares
findings.mitigation: revert on zero-share deposits; seed dead shares at vault creation
findings.phase2_reclassification: Same root cause, now measured, bounded and traced to the missing minDeposit guard.

findings.title: An uninitialized clone can be seized by the first initialize() caller
findings.root_cause: initialize() has no access control; MaonoVaultFactory_Phase1B clones and initializes atomically, so the window does not exist today
findings.mitigation: restrict initialize() to the factory address
findings.phase2_reclassification: Unchanged: the factory initializes clones atomically.

findings.title: Two divergent MaonoVault contracts; the deployed one has no source in the repository
findings.mitigation: commit the deployed contract's source, verify bytecode, and converge on one vault model
findings.phase2_reclassification: There was one contract and one stale build artifact, not two vaults. The artifact is now generated from source and parity-tested by test/security/phase2/ArtifactParity.t.sol.

findings.title: Monthly upkeep is unenforceable and the payer sets its own price
findings.violated_invariant: the protocol collects the fee it advertises
findings.root_cause: collectMonthlyUpkeep() is onlyOwner with no accrued liability, and the three inputs to the invoice (UPKEEP_COSTS_MONTHLY, BURN_PERCENTAGES, daoTreasury) all have onlyOwner setters on the same contract, callable in the same transaction as the payment. Skipped months are never back-charged and the clock advances from payment time rather than due time.

economics.compliant_owner_actually_pays: 133.65 MTAA (the discount curve applies to the owner's own float)
economics.late_payments_every_45_days: 9 chargeable periods per year instead of 12
economics.silence: 0 MTAA, vault stays ACTIVE for 10 years
economics.setUpkeepCostAt_zero: 0 MTAA, no burn, hibernation becomes unreachable
economics.setDaoTreasury_self_investing_vault: 70% returned to the payer; net cost is the burn only
economics.burn_zero_plus_redirect: 0 MTAA real cost while the vault books paid > 0

findings.mitigation: hold the fee schedule, burn split and treasury at the factory/platform level rather than per-vault behind the vault owner's onlyOwner; accrue skipped months, or let anyone trigger collectMonthlyUpkeep() for a delinquent vault

findings.title: Hibernation is cheaper than compliance and freezes depositors at zero cost
findings.violated_invariant: delinquency costs more than compliance; depositors can exit a solvent vault
findings.root_cause: the reactivation fee is 1.5x one month regardless of how long the vault hibernated, and is priced from the owner-settable table at reactivation time; there is no timeout, guardian or depositor escape hatch
findings.mitigation: scale the reactivation fee with the number of hibernated months, bound the freeze, and allow anyone (or the depositors) to pay for reactivation

findings.title: Deposits below the share price mint zero shares and are silently absorbed
findings.actor: any depositor; an attacker cannot profit
findings.violated_invariant: a successful deposit gives the depositor a claim
findings.root_cause: the canonical vault has no minimum deposit (the legacy artifact did); the virtual-share offset shifts the threshold but does not remove it, so once the share price exceeds the deposit, deposit() keeps the assets and mints nothing

economics.attacker_profit: 0 - the incumbents' gain never exceeds the seeding cost
economics.fuzzed_statement: victimLoss > dust implies attackerLoss > victimLoss, 512/512 cases
economics.realistic_exposure: an honest user in a vault whose price rose legitimately

findings.mitigation: revert when shares == 0, or restore a minDeposit; note that previewDeposit() already returns 0 so integrators can refuse the call, while maxDeposit() still advertises the vault as open

findings.title: Upkeep paid while hibernating is charged but does not reactivate the vault
findings.root_cause: collectMonthlyUpkeep() carries no onlyActive guard, so it charges while the status is HIBERNATING and leaves the status unchanged
findings.mitigation: add onlyActive to collectMonthlyUpkeep, or credit the payment against the reactivation fee

findings.title: Donations to an empty or near-empty vault are permanently stranded
findings.violated_invariant: none - this is the cost of the inflation defence
findings.root_cause: a donation is split between the real shares and the 1000 virtual shares; with no or tiny real supply, nearly all of it backs shares that nobody owns

economics.donation_to_share_less_vault: fully unattributable; a later depositor recovers only part of it

findings.mitigation: none required; documented so that invariant I7 is stated correctly

findings.title: MAX_SPAWN_COST_MTAA is unreachable and the spawn-cost view is owner-repointable
findings.root_cause: the oracle reports whole USD cents, so the cheapest representable price already quotes 500 MTAA, a quarter of the ceiling; only the floor clamp can bind. The oracle address is owner-settable, so the view is owner-influenced within the clamps

economics.share_accounting_impact: none - the oracle never touches ERC-4626 math
economics.integration_impact: an integrator reading spawn pricing from a vault rather than the factory reads an owner-influenced number, floor-clamped at MIN_SPAWN_COST_MTAA

findings.mitigation: widen the oracle precision or drop the dead ceiling clamp; integrators should read spawn pricing from the factory

findings.title: Deploy scripts and backend target a contract shape that no longer exists
findings.violated_invariant: the integration layer's contract API matches the canonical ABI
findings.root_cause: the deploy path calls factory.deploy(asset, daoTreasury, manager) while MaonoVault_Phase1B is a clone+initialize contract whose implementation calls _disableInitializers(); the backend calls previewNAV(), updateNAV() and distributePerformanceFee(), none of which exist in the canonical ABI

economics.impact: the deploy path cannot produce a working vault and every automation call reverts

findings.mitigation: run node scripts/build-maono-artifact.mjs --check in CI, replace the constructor deploy path with clone+initialize, and remove or rewrite the NAV/performance-fee automation

negative_results.reason: _decimalsOffset()=3 virtual shares; attacker cost exceeded victim loss by ~1098x (18-dec case) and in all 512 fuzz cases
donation accrues pro-rata to all holders including the victim; attacker exited 1 wei below capital
rounding always favours the vault across 200 repeated round trips and 512 fuzz cases
nonReentrant on all four ERC-4626 entry points and both upkeep functions
totalAssets() is the raw balance; donations only reprice shares upward
rejected by SafeERC20
all setters revert for unprivileged callers; Ownable2Step handover cannot be hijacked
initializer modifier and _disableInitializers()
the oracle only feeds getSpawnCostInMTAA(); bounded and try/catch-wrapped
totalAssets() ignores lastNAV
shares checked and burned at fulfilment; redeem-first, transfer-first and stacked-request variants all ended at exactly the starting capital
fees accrue pro-rata over time; an immediate second call collects 0
setPerformanceFee/setManagementFee are capped
collectMonthlyUpkeep() is onlyOwner
no code path sets it (dead state)

negative_results.attack: Donation before/after another depositor (fuzzed ordering and sizes)
negative_results.reason: the donor funds the whole discount; donor never profits and the victim never loses more than a zero-share deposit, 512/512 cases

negative_results.attack: Donation sandwich around a victim deposit
negative_results.reason: the victim mints fewer but proportionally more valuable shares; the donor recovers only its own donation
losses compound for the donor

negative_results.attack: 250 dust deposit/redeem cycles at a donated share price
negative_results.reason: rounding always favours the vault; no accumulation into profit
no per-block accumulator exists; same-block is indistinguishable from spread-out activity

negative_results.attack: Mixed-magnitude deposits (1 wei .. 1e18) with reverse-order exits
negative_results.reason: nobody extracted more than they deposited; at most 6 wei stranded

negative_results.attack: Exhaustive owner-only entry points, including selectors that do not exist
negative_results.reason: no owner path moves the underlying asset; the canonical vault has no emergencyWithdraw/sweep/rescue

negative_results.attack: Depositor buying its own way out of hibernation
negative_results.reason: reactivateFromHibernation is onlyOwner; MTAA in a depositor's hands does not help (liveness finding P2-2)

negative_results.attack: Timing a call around a pause/hibernation transition to obtain a different price
negative_results.reason: guarded calls are rejected outright, never executed at a different price; transitions are price-neutral

negative_results.attack: Double-charging upkeep in one block; reaching the CLOSED status
negative_results.reason: UpkeepNotDue guards repeats; no function writes CLOSED

negative_results.attack: Overflowing the upkeep clock or hibernation counter
negative_results.reason: clean at uint64.max and after a century of hibernation

negative_results.attack: Stateful random sequences of all nine user and owner actions (4096 calls per invariant)
negative_results.reason: eight economic invariants held, including conservation (totalAssets == totalIn - totalOut) and totalOut <= totalIn
